statusDetail: Complete 58-check audit of the public Google Meet marketing landing page reached through meet.google.com. Authenticated meeting rooms and Google Account flows were not covered.

page.notes: meet.google.com redirects through meet.google.com/about and apps.google.com/meet/ to workspace.google.com/products/meet/. The accessible surface is a long public marketing page; authenticated Meet is behind Google Accounts.

paths.description: Public Meet product landing page and its primary Go to app boundary; representative of the one accessible marketing template. Tested desktop/mobile, preference media, keyboard focus, lead-form invalid submission, no-JS crawler view, load/network, security, and memory. Not covered: authenticated meeting room, account settings, pricing/checkout, or live call media because they require credentials and participants.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark colour-scheme preference
findings.evidence: Dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; computed html/body color-scheme is normal and surfaces remain white.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and preference-driven surface/text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The very long page offers no scroll-state-aware orientation
findings.evidence: The 10,577px page retains static chrome and the probe found no scroll timeline; no progress or scroll-state response is exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight declarative progress/section-state cue for this long marketing page.

findings.summary: Cookie consent obscures the primary content on load
findings.evidence: Initial desktop capture shows the cookie panel covering the hero heading; at 360x800 it consumes roughly the bottom 35% of the viewport. The panel is not exposed as dialog/popover in the probed DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, semantic consent surface that preserves access to the hero, supports keyboard dismissal, and does not consume a third of mobile height.

findings.summary: Several in-page navigation links have no visible keyboard focus
findings.evidence: Focus probe found section links such as Gemini in Meet, Flexible, Enhance, and FAQ with outline none and no box shadow while focused.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a high-contrast :focus-visible ring with adequate offset to every interactive section link.

findings.summary: Required-field errors are not announced as system state
findings.evidence: Submitting the empty required lead form produced invalid custom fields but the probe found no role=alert or non-empty aria-live announcement.
findings.suggestedFix: After attempted submission, associate field messages and announce a concise error summary through role=alert or aria-live.

findings.summary: Cold mobile loading misses the Core Web Vitals performance bar
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 12.3s, FCP 5.0s, TTI 12.3s, and performance 0.56. A warm trace was better at LCP 2.33s, so cold-load risk is the actionable result.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the redirect chain, prioritize the LCP asset, and defer non-critical scripts/styles; verify mobile LCP under 2.5s.

findings.summary: Redirects, render-blocking resources, and unused code inflate delivery
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 119 requests and 2,536,409 transferred bytes after three redirects; Lighthouse estimated 140 KiB unused JS, 26 KiB unused CSS, and 1.5s render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the canonical page directly, inline or consolidate critical CSS, defer analytics, and remove unused JS/CSS.

findings.summary: Visible labels and accessible names disagree on nine controls
findings.evidence: Lighthouse label-content-name-mismatch found 9 controls, including visible “Go to app” links named “Sign in to Google Meet” and tooltip/language controls whose visible text is absent from the accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Make each accessible name include its visible label; do not label “Go to app” only as “Sign in to Google Meet”.

findings.summary: The page exposes two H1 headings
findings.evidence: DOM probe found two H1 elements on one page: “Video conferencing for business” and “Video calls, enhanced with AI”.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one page-level H1 and demote the alternate responsive/variant heading without changing its visual styling.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 13 non-descriptive links, including repeated “Learn more” labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace generic “Learn more” labels with destination-specific text or accessible context that also helps crawlers.

findings.summary: Canonical and redirect indexing signals are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Lighthouse canonical audit failed; the requested meet.google.com URL redirects through three hosts while canonical points to /intl/en_uk/products/meet/.
findings.suggestedFix: Redirect meet.google.com directly to the localized canonical URL and ensure the emitted canonical matches the final indexable URL.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP posture leave avoidable security gaps
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS and nonce-based CSP, but CSP allows unsafe-eval; the NID cookie was reported Secure=false and SameSite=None on an HTTPS page.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure NID is Secure with an intentional SameSite policy and eliminate unsafe-eval from the CSP where possible.

findings.summary: The landing page has a large analytics and third-party footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 10 third-party origins and active Tag Manager plus two Google Analytics origins; HAR attributes 2,533,170 of 2,536,409 bytes to origins other than the requested meet.google.com origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate analytics on consent, reduce tags and events to the minimum needed, and serve performance-critical assets from the canonical origin where practical.

findings.summary: Clickjacking and browser-policy headers are incomplete
findings.evidence: Header capture found no frame-ancestors directive or X-Frame-Options, and no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; retain HSTS and nosniff.

findings.summary: The lead form does not expose autocomplete tokens
findings.evidence: All visible lead fields in the DOM probe, including first name, last name, email, company, and job title, had empty autocomplete values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add name, given-name, family-name, email, organization, organization-title, and tel autocomplete tokens as appropriate.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes an estimated 280 KiB
findings.evidence: Lighthouse image-delivery insight estimated 280 KiB savings; the HAR’s largest image is 616,278 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve tighter responsive variants in modern formats and ensure the LCP image is correctly sized and prioritized.

findings.summary: Fonts and analytics are disproportionate to the landing-page task
findings.evidence: HAR loaded 534,442 bytes of fonts, 341 KiB of Tag Manager scripts, and 116 origin-mismatched requests; Lighthouse estimated about 140 KiB of those analytics scripts unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset/consolidate fonts, defer analytics until consent/idle, and enforce a third-party byte/request budget.
